summary: Sets out requirements for infrastructure, or carrier, ENUM, which uses ENUM (RFC 3761) technology to help networks interconnect for services addressed by telephone numbers, especially voice over IP. It is informational and describes requirements, not a protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: Infrastructure ENUM lets a telephone carrier publish where another network can connect to deliver service for a phone number. RFC 5067 lists requirements for such a system; it does not define the system itself.

questions: what does carrier of record mean
how does infrastructure enum connect carriers
subtitle: Requirements for carriers to publish network interconnection information using ENUM.

tldr.problem: Carriers need ways to interconnect networks that deliver services addressed by E.164 telephone numbers, including voice over IP.
tldr.mechanism: Infrastructure ENUM uses RFC 3761 technology for a carrier-of-record to publish a URI identifying a point of interconnection for a number. This RFC lists requirements, not a complete protocol.
tldr.outcome: The requirements cover a common DNS namespace, query responses, URIs, privacy, reliability, and compatibility with end-user ENUM.

facts.label: Published mapping
facts.value: Number to a URI identifying an interconnection point

today: RFC 5067 is Informational and the supplied metadata lists no RFC that updates or obsoletes it.

sections.title: Carrier ENUM and the Carrier of Record
sections.content:
Infrastructure ENUM applies the ENUM technology of RFC 3761 to publish a mapping from an E.164 number to a URI identifying a point of interconnection with a service provider's network. The mapping is separate from any URI an end user may choose to associate with the number.

The carrier-of-record controls the infrastructure ENUM domain and its records. Depending on the numbering arrangement, this may be the provider to which a number was allocated, the provider to which it was ported, or a provider selected by the end user as an interconnection point.
sections.plainLanguage: End-user ENUM can associate a phone number with an end user's chosen address. Infrastructure ENUM instead tells carriers where to connect to reach the provider responsible for that number.

sections.title: Why Carriers Need Infrastructure ENUM
sections.content:
Voice providers use E.164 numbers as naming and routing information. Infrastructure ENUM can link those numbers to Internet-based resources, allowing providers to peer using IP protocols as well as, or instead of, connecting through traditional telephone networks.

A provider may publish numbers or number ranges it hosts even when the final user's device is on a private IP network or a traditional telephone network, provided an Internet-accessible point into the provider network exists. The RFC notes that additional peering and accounting agreements may be needed, and a query alone does not guarantee that the caller can reach the destination network.
sections.plainLanguage: Carriers can use a number lookup to find an Internet-based entry point into another provider's network. A successful lookup does not itself provide permission or guarantee that the networks can connect.

sections.title: Requirements for the Namespace and Queries
sections.content:
The system must let providers publish DNS records for their numbers in one common, publicly accessible namespace. Queries for infrastructure ENUM names must return a result, including a refusal response when appropriate, and records must be able to provide a URI for delivery to the carrier-of-record.

The requirements also call for name-server performance comparable to Internet root name servers, support for end-user choice of ENUM registrar, and compatibility with open or closed numbering plans and private ENUM trees. Resolver changes should be minimized, and lookups should be kept efficient.
sections.plainLanguage: Providers need a shared place to publish interconnection records, and queries need a response. The design should work alongside end-user ENUM without limiting an end user's registrar choice.

sections.title: Privacy and Security
sections.content:
A public record for only assigned numbers could reveal unlisted numbers when compared with directories. The RFC suggests registering all numbers allocated to a provider, including unassigned numbers, and routing them in the same way before indicating that a number is unassigned.

Returned URIs should not expose unnecessary user identity. The RFC also says infrastructure ENUM implementations should reconsider the RFC 3761 security model because carriers, rather than individual end users, control the records in this setting.
sections.plainLanguage: Publishing only active numbers could reveal which numbers are private or unlisted. Registering the full allocated range in the same way can reduce that information leak.
